summary: Sumatriptan is a selective serotonin 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist (triptan) for the acute treatment of migraine (with or without aura) and, for the subcutaneous form, cluster headache. It is not used for prophylaxis. It is available subcutaneously (6 mg, max 12 mg/24h), orally (25-100 mg, may repeat after 2 hours, max 200 mg/24h), and intranasally (5-20 mg). Its therapeutic effect is attributed to cranial vasoconstriction and inhibition of pro-inflammatory neuropeptide release from trigeminal sensory nerves. It is contraindicated in ischemic coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, certain arrhythmia/accessory-pathway syndromes, and hemiplegic/basilar migraine, and must not be combined with ergot derivatives or another triptan within 24 hours, or with an MAOI-A (or within 2 weeks of stopping one for oral/nasal forms). Serotonin syndrome can occur, especially with other serotonergic agents.
indications: Acute treatment of migraine, with or without aura, in adults (oral, subcutaneous, intranasal)
Acute treatment of cluster headache in adults (subcutaneous form)

dosage.d: 6 mg single dose; if needed a second dose >=1 hour later; maximum 12 mg in 24 hours
dosage.t: Lower doses (1-5 mg) may be used if 6 mg side effects are dose-limiting

dosage.d: 25, 50, or 100 mg single dose; may repeat after 2 hours if partial response; maximum 200 mg in 24 hours
dosage.t: 100 mg is the maximum single oral dose
dosage.n: If no response to first dose, a second dose is unlikely to help

dosage.d: 5, 10, or 20 mg in one nostril; may repeat after 2 hours; maximum 40 mg in 24 hours
dosage.t: Nasal powder device dosing differs (e.g. 22 mg)

dosage.d: 6 mg single dose; maximum 12 mg in 24 hours with doses separated by >=1 hour
dosage.t: SC route only for cluster headache

admin: Take/administer as early as possible after the migraine attack begins (it can be used at any point during an attack)
Do not exceed the route-specific 24-hour maximum; separate repeat doses by at least 1 hour (SC) or 2 hours (oral/nasal)
Assess cardiovascular risk before the first dose; consider giving the first dose under medical supervision in at-risk patients and obtaining an ECG
Do not use within 24 hours of an ergotamine-containing or ergot-type medication or another 5-HT1 agonist (triptan)
Do not use the oral/nasal forms with, or within 2 weeks of, an MAO-A inhibitor
For subcutaneous use, rotate injection sites; patients can self-inject with the autoinjector after training
moa: Sumatriptan binds with high affinity to 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors. It is thought to relieve migraine and cluster headache through agonist activity at these receptors located on intracranial (including the basilar artery and dura mater) blood vessels and on sensory nerves of the trigeminal system. Stimulation produces vasoconstriction of dilated cranial vessels and inhibits the release of pro-inflammatory and vasoactive neuropeptides (such as CGRP and substance P) from trigeminal nerve endings, reducing neurogenic inflammation and the transmission of pain signals. It has little affinity for 5-HT2, 5-HT3, adrenergic, dopaminergic, muscarinic, or benzodiazepine receptors.

absolute: Ischemic coronary artery disease (angina, prior MI, documented silent ischemia) or coronary vasospasm including Prinzmetal's angina
History of stroke or transient ischemic attack
Peripheral vascular disease (including ischemic bowel disease)
Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome or arrhythmias with other accessory conduction pathway disorders
Use within 24 hours of ergotamine/ergot-type medication or another 5-HT1 agonist (triptan)
Concurrent or recent (within 2 weeks) MAO-A inhibitor (oral and intranasal forms)
relative: Cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes, smoking, obesity, strong family history, postmenopausal women, men >40) - assess before use
Concurrent serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, other triptans) - serotonin syndrome risk
Seizure disorder or conditions lowering seizure threshold
monitor: Cardiovascular symptoms (chest/throat/jaw tightness or pain) after dosing
Signs of serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, tremor, clonus, autonomic instability)

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; available data have not shown a clear increased risk of major birth defects. Use sumatriptan during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. A pregnancy registry historically collected outcomes of exposed pregnancies.
lact: Sumatriptan is excreted in human breast milk. Infant exposure can be minimised by avoiding breastfeeding for about 12 hours after a dose (and discarding milk during that period). Use with caution and weigh benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's need for the drug.
renal: Pharmacokinetics in renal impairment have not been extensively characterised; use with caution. No specific oral dose adjustment is firmly established, but reduced clearance may warrant lower doses and careful monitoring in significant impairment.
hepatic: Hepatic metabolism (first-pass) is significant for oral sumatriptan. In mild to moderate hepatic impairment, plasma concentrations are increased - limit the maximum single oral dose to 50 mg. Sumatriptan is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Ergotamine / dihydroergotamine and other ergot-type medications (additive prolonged vasospasm - do not use within 24 hours)
Other 5-HT1 agonists / triptans (additive vasospastic effects - separate by 24 hours)
MAO-A inhibitors (increase sumatriptan exposure - contraindicated with oral/nasal forms; avoid within 2 weeks of stopping)
moderate: Tricyclic antidepressants, lithium, tramadol, St John's Wort (additive serotonergic effect)
minor: No significant CYP-based drug interactions of clinical note for most agents
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction; tablets may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No direct pharmacologic interaction, but alcohol can precipitate migraine
interactions.diagnostics: Transient blood-pressure elevation may occur; no specific lab interference

common: Feeling of pressure, tightness, or heaviness (chest, throat, neck, jaw)
serious: Coronary artery vasospasm / myocardial ischemia or infarction
Peripheral and gastrointestinal vasospasm (ischemic colitis, Raynaud-like)

monitoring: Cardiovascular risk assessment before the first dose; consider ECG/supervised first dose in at-risk patients
Symptoms after dosing: chest/jaw/throat tightness, palpitations (possible cardiac ischemia)
Signs of serotonin syndrome when combined with serotonergic drugs
Frequency of headache and triptan use (medication-overuse headache)
counsel: Use this only to treat a migraine (or cluster headache) attack - it does not prevent attacks
Take it as soon as the headache starts; do not exceed the daily maximum for your form
Stop and seek urgent care if you get chest, jaw, throat, or arm tightness/pain, or palpitations
Do not use within 24 hours of an ergot medicine or another triptan
Tell your doctor about antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs) - combined use can cause serotonin syndrome
Using it on too many days per month can cause rebound (medication-overuse) headaches
For the injection, follow the autoinjector training and rotate sites; for the nasal spray, expect a brief bad taste
pk: Subcutaneous: ~10 minutes; oral/nasal: ~30 minutes to 1-2 hours
SC peak ~12 minutes; oral Tmax ~1-1.5 h (delayed during an attack); intranasal ~1-1.5 h
Headache relief over ~2-4 hours; headache can recur, allowing a repeat dose
Store at 20-25 degrees C (excursions 15-30 degrees C); protect from light; do not freeze injection
pearls: Acute therapy only - not for migraine prophylaxis; if the first dose fails, a second dose for the same attack is usually ineffective (oral).
Contraindicated in ischemic coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, WPW/accessory-pathway arrhythmias, and hemiplegic/basilar migraine.
Do not combine with ergots or another triptan within 24 hours; oral/nasal forms are contraindicated with MAO-A inhibitors (and within 2 weeks of stopping).
Serotonin syndrome can occur, particularly with SSRIs/SNRIs - counsel and monitor.
Frequent use causes medication-overuse headache; limit treatment days per month.
Hepatic dosing: limit oral single dose to 50 mg in mild-moderate impairment; contraindicated in severe impairment. SC is the fastest-onset route and the only form for cluster headache.
missed: Not applicable as a scheduled medicine - sumatriptan is taken as needed for an acute attack. Do not take extra doses to 'catch up', and do not exceed the maximum dose in 24 hours. If your headaches are frequent, discuss preventive treatment with your doctor.
overdose: Overdose may cause tremor, convulsions, hyperaemia (redness), lethargy, paralysis, and cardiovascular effects including marked vasoconstriction, hypertension, and potential ischemia. There is no specific antidote. Manage supportively with continuous monitoring of cardiovascular and neurological status for at least 10-12 hours and treat symptomatically. The effect of haemodialysis/peritoneal dialysis on plasma levels is unknown.
